To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we report two novel mutations in KIF1A that are located outside the motor domain and that are associated with autosomal recessive hereditary spastic gait disorder.

two affected siblings with hereditary spastic gait disorder and additional neurological symptoms have been diagnosed with SPG30 caused by compound hetero-zygous mutations outside of the motor domain of KIF1A.
we report a family of Macedonian descent with two affected siblings with a slowly progressive and a more complex and rapid progressing hereditary spatic paraplegia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular basis of hereditary spastice paraplegia in a family with a complex phenotype.
the identification of novel mutations in the KIFIA gene in a family with autosomal recessive hereditary spasticity.
the identification of the genetic cause in a family with a complex form of recessive hereditary spasticity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the KIF1 gene should be included in the diagnostic workup of patients with a suspected diagnosis of autosomal-recessive hereditary spasticity.
mutations in KIF1A are responsible for both autosomal dominant and recessive forms of SPG30.
KIF1A mutations are a rare cause of hereditary spastis paraplegia and that they can cause a pure or a complex phenotype.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
KIF1A is a gene that is associated with autosomal dominant as well as autosomal recessive forms of hereditary motor neuron disease.
the KIF1a gene is a candidate for autosomal recessive spastic paraparesis and it is a candidate gene for other forms of spastic parapresis as well.
the motor domain is not necessary for the function of KIF1A, but it seems that the mutations outside the motor are less severe and therefore cause a milder phenotype.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the KIF1 gene should be included in the genetic screening for patients with a complex form of hereditary spatic paraplegia, and the motor domain is probably not the only region of the gene that is important for the pathogenesis of the disease.

the motor domain of KIF1A is not the only region that can be mutated in hereditary spasticity, and therefore, the diagnosis of SPG30 should be considered in patients presenting with spastic paraparesis and additional neurological symptoms, especially if the disease is of recessive inheritance.
